newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -BUNDS IN NARROW RANGE, 102.51 TO CAP.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -BUNDS IN NARROW RANGE, 102.51 TO CAP.

text.p: September Bund futures on LIFFE will be confined to a one point range on Friday bordered by 101.50 on the downside and 102.51 at most on the upside, technical analysts said.
But any trading action above the August 6 low at 101.50 will be corrective ahead of another move down, they added.

"For the short term, we're still in a correction from the 101.50 low," said Robin Wilkin, senior technical analyst at MCM YieldWatch in London. "If we do manage to break through yesterday's high at 102.17, then we'll probably try to push up initially to 102.32, the August 5 peak."

Wilkin said above there, the market would aim for 102.51, the 50 percent retracement of the recent move down from 103.51 on July 31. "We shouldn't go any higher than there, I'm looking for it to top out around there," he said.
By 0712 GMT, September Bunds on LIFFE were down one basis point at 102.01.
Wilkin said a failure to push through Thursday's high and a move down through 101.80, the low so far this session, would put pressure on 101.50.
"Until we get through there, we may still see a bit of sideways action ahead of a return to a bear trend," he said.
Wilkin's medium term target was 100.93, the 62 percent retracement of the move from 99.32, the low on May 29, to 103.52, the contract high made on July 23.
"All the action over 101.50 is corrective ahead of a move to the 100.93 area," he said.
Tim Hampton, head of futures sales at the Royal Bank of Scotland, said Bunds needed a move above 102.20 to regain their bull run, with a close above 102.35 "the best possible outcome".
He said the contract was very well supported at the 101.49 trendline and 101.47 retracement level.
By 0730 GMT, December Euromarks were up 0.04 at 96.52.
